subject: Physics
question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² for 5 seconds. What is the distance covered?
detailed_solution: Using s = ut + ½at². u=0, a=4 m/s², t=5s. s = 0 + ½ × 4 × 25 = 50 m.
formula_or_concept: s = ut + ½at² (second equation of motion)
common_mistakes: Forgetting to halve the acceleration term
Using v=u+at instead of displacement equation
ai_explanation_seed: Uniform acceleration from rest; apply second equation of motion directly.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally with velocity 20 m/s from a height of 80 m. What is the horizontal range? (g = 10 m/s²)
detailed_solution: Time to fall: h = ½gt² → 80 = ½×10×t² → t = 4 s. Range = u×t = 20×4 = 80 m.
formula_or_concept: Time of flight from free fall; horizontal range = horizontal velocity × time
common_mistakes: Using projectile formula for range (only valid for equal height launch/land)
Forgetting to calculate time first
ai_explanation_seed: Horizontal throw: vertical motion is free fall, horizontal is uniform. Find time from vertical, then horizontal range.

subject: Physics
question_text: Train A moves east at 60 km/h and train B moves west at 90 km/h on parallel tracks. What is the speed of B relative to A?
detailed_solution: Taking east as positive: v_A = +60, v_B = -90. Relative velocity of B w.r.t. A = v_B - v_A = -90 - 60 = -150 km/h. Speed = 150 km/h.
formula_or_concept: Relative velocity: v_BA = v_B - v_A
common_mistakes: Subtracting speeds instead of using sign convention for direction
Confusing which velocity to subtract from which
ai_explanation_seed: Relative velocity requires sign convention. Opposite directions means speeds add up.

subject: Physics
question_text: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
detailed_solution: Area under v-t graph = ∫v dt = displacement. The slope of v-t graph gives acceleration.
formula_or_concept: Area under v-t graph = displacement; slope of v-t graph = acceleration
common_mistakes: Confusing slope (acceleration) with area (displacement)
Saying distance instead of displacement
ai_explanation_seed: Integral of velocity with respect to time is displacement. This is a fundamental calculus-kinematics connection.

subject: Physics
question_text: A particle starts from rest and moves with acceleration a = (2t + 1) m/s². What is its velocity at t = 3 s?
detailed_solution: a = dv/dt = 2t + 1. Integrating: v = t² + t + C. At t=0, v=0 → C=0. At t=3: v = 9 + 3 = 12 m/s.
formula_or_concept: Variable acceleration: a = dv/dt; integrate to find velocity
common_mistakes: Using constant-acceleration equations for variable acceleration
Forgetting the integration constant and applying initial conditions
ai_explanation_seed: Variable acceleration requires calculus. Integrate a = dv/dt with respect to time and apply initial conditions.

subject: Physics
question_text: A net force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4 kg. What is the acceleration produced?
detailed_solution: F = ma → a = F/m = 20/4 = 5 m/s².
formula_or_concept: Newton's Second Law: F = ma
common_mistakes: Dividing mass by force instead of force by mass
Forgetting units
ai_explanation_seed: Direct application of Newton's second law. F=ma → a=F/m.

subject: Physics
question_text: A block of mass 5 kg is on a surface with μ = 0.3. What minimum force (horizontal) is needed to move it? (g = 10 m/s²)
detailed_solution: Normal force N = mg = 5×10 = 50 N. Maximum static friction = μN = 0.3×50 = 15 N. Applied force must exceed 15 N to cause motion; minimum = 15 N (just overcome static friction).
formula_or_concept: f_s(max) = μₛN; object moves when applied force > maximum static friction
common_mistakes: Using kinetic friction coefficient when asking about starting motion
Forgetting to calculate normal force first
ai_explanation_seed: To just start motion, applied force must equal maximum static friction. Calculate N = mg, then f_max = μN.

subject: Physics
question_text: In an Atwood machine, masses 3 kg and 5 kg are connected by a string over a frictionless pulley. What is the acceleration of the system? (g = 10 m/s²)
formula_or_concept: Atwood machine acceleration: a = (m₂ - m₁)g / (m₁ + m₂)
common_mistakes: Not accounting for both masses in denominator
Using net mass difference only without summing total mass
ai_explanation_seed: Apply Newton's second law to each mass separately, then solve simultaneous equations. Net force = difference in weights; total inertia = sum of masses.

subject: Physics
question_text: A car moves in a circular path of radius 100 m at 20 m/s. What is the centripetal acceleration?
formula_or_concept: Centripetal acceleration: a_c = v²/r = ω²r
common_mistakes: Using a = v/r instead of v²/r
Confusing centripetal acceleration with tangential acceleration
ai_explanation_seed: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r. Direction is toward the center of the circle.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg moving at 10 m/s hits a wall and rebounds at 8 m/s. What is the impulse on the ball?
detailed_solution: Impulse = Δp = m(v_f - v_i). Taking initial direction as positive: v_i = +10, v_f = -8. Δp = 0.5×(-8-10) = 0.5×(-18) = -9 N·s. Magnitude = 9 N·s.
formula_or_concept: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v_f - v_i); direction matters
common_mistakes: Forgetting that rebound velocity is negative (opposite direction)
Computing 0.5×(10-8) = 1 N·s ignoring sign
ai_explanation_seed: Impulse is vector quantity. Rebound means velocity reverses sign. Impulse = m(v_f - v_i) with signs.

subject: Physics
question_text: A force of 50 N displaces an object by 6 m at 60° to the direction of force. What is the work done?
formula_or_concept: W = F·d·cosθ; work depends on component of force along displacement
common_mistakes: Using sinθ instead of cosθ
Ignoring the angle and computing F×d directly
ai_explanation_seed: Work is the dot product of force and displacement. Only the component of force along the displacement does work.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
detailed_solution: By conservation of energy: KE = Loss in PE = mgh = 2×10×10 = 200 J.
formula_or_concept: Conservation of mechanical energy: KE gained = PE lost = mgh
common_mistakes: Computing KE = ½mv² without finding v first
Using wrong formula for PE
ai_explanation_seed: Energy conservation: all potential energy converts to kinetic energy when dropped from rest.

subject: Physics
question_text: A motor lifts a 200 kg load to a height of 20 m in 40 s. What is the power of the motor? (g = 10 m/s²)
formula_or_concept: Power = Work/time = Fv
common_mistakes: Forgetting to include g in weight calculation
Dividing by mass instead of time
ai_explanation_seed: Power is the rate of doing work. Calculate work first (W=mgh), then divide by time.

subject: Physics
question_text: 800 J of heat is supplied to a gas and the gas does 300 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?
detailed_solution: ΔU = Q - W = 800 - 300 = 500 J. (First Law: Q = ΔU + W)
formula_or_concept: First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔU = Q - W
common_mistakes: Adding Q and W instead of subtracting
Confusing sign conventions (W done by gas is positive here)
ai_explanation_seed: First Law: heat added equals increase in internal energy plus work done by gas. ΔU = Q - W.

subject: Physics
question_text: At constant temperature, a gas at 2 atm occupies 4 L. What volume does it occupy at 8 atm?
detailed_solution: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. 2×4 = 8×V₂ → V₂ = 8/8 = 1 L.
formula_or_concept: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (at constant T)
common_mistakes: Using P₁/V₁ = P₂/V₂ (inverse relationship is P₁V₁ = P₂V₂)
Confusing Boyle's with Charles's Law
ai_explanation_seed: Boyle's Law: pressure and volume are inversely proportional at constant temperature.

subject: Physics
question_text: A Carnot engine operates between 500 K and 300 K. What is its efficiency?
formula_or_concept: Carnot efficiency: η = 1 - T_L/T_H (temperatures in Kelvin)
common_mistakes: Using Celsius instead of Kelvin
Computing T_hot/T_cold instead of T_cold/T_hot
ai_explanation_seed: Carnot efficiency = 1 - T_cold/T_hot. Always use Kelvin. Maximum possible efficiency between two reservoirs.

subject: Physics
question_text: How much heat is required to raise 2 kg of water from 20°C to 70°C? (Specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg·K)
formula_or_concept: Q = mcΔT where c is specific heat capacity
common_mistakes: Using temperature values instead of temperature difference
Forgetting to multiply by mass
ai_explanation_seed: Heat transferred Q = mcΔT. Calculate temperature change ΔT first, then multiply by mass and specific heat.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two charges of +4 μC and -4 μC are separated by 2 m. How does the force change if the separation is halved?
detailed_solution: F ∝ 1/r². If r → r/2, F → F × (r/(r/2))² = F × 4. Force quadruples.
formula_or_concept: Coulomb's Law: F = kq₁q₂/r²; force varies inversely as square of distance
common_mistakes: Thinking force doubles when distance halves (linear thinking)
Not applying inverse square correctly
ai_explanation_seed: Inverse square law: halving distance → distance factor of (1/2)² = 1/4 in denominator → force multiplies by 4.

subject: Physics
question_text: The electric potential at a point 0.3 m from a charge of 3×10⁻⁹ C is (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²):
formula_or_concept: Electric potential: V = kq/r (scalar quantity)
common_mistakes: Using the field formula E = kq/r² instead of potential V = kq/r
Getting the exponent arithmetic wrong
ai_explanation_seed: Electric potential V = kq/r. Note it's 1/r (not 1/r² like the field).

subject: Physics
question_text: Two capacitors of 4 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. What is the equivalent capacitance?
formula_or_concept: Series capacitors: 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ (opposite of resistors!)
common_mistakes: Using C₁+C₂ formula (parallel, not series)
Inverting the final answer
ai_explanation_seed: Series capacitors: reciprocals add (like parallel resistors). In series, capacitance decreases.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows?
formula_or_concept: Ohm's Law: V = IR → I = V/R
common_mistakes: Inverting: I = R/V
Unit errors
ai_explanation_seed: Basic Ohm's Law: current = voltage divided by resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
formula_or_concept: Parallel resistors: 1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃
common_mistakes: Adding resistances directly (series formula)
Arithmetic errors in fractions
ai_explanation_seed: Parallel resistors: conductances add. 1/R_eq = sum of 1/each R.

subject: Physics
question_text: In a circuit, two branches carry 3 A and 5 A toward a junction. What current leaves the junction through the third branch?
detailed_solution: By Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): sum of currents entering = sum leaving. 3 + 5 = 8 A leaves through third branch.
formula_or_concept: KCL: ΣI_in = ΣI_out at any junction
common_mistakes: Subtracting currents instead of adding for KCL
Confusing KCL with KVL
ai_explanation_seed: Kirchhoff's Current Law: charge conservation means total current in equals total current out at any node.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 0.5 m wire carrying 4 A current is placed perpendicular to a 0.3 T magnetic field. What is the force on the wire?
formula_or_concept: Force on current-carrying conductor: F = BIL sinθ
common_mistakes: Forgetting sinθ factor (=1 for perpendicular)
Getting order of multiplication wrong
ai_explanation_seed: F = BIL sinθ. Perpendicular means θ = 90°, sinθ = 1. Multiply B, I, L.

subject: Physics
question_text: A coil has 100 turns and the magnetic flux through it changes from 0.02 Wb to 0.08 Wb in 0.3 s. What is the induced EMF?
formula_or_concept: Faraday's Law: EMF = -N(dΦ/dt); magnitude = N × ΔΦ/Δt
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply by number of turns N
Dividing flux change incorrectly
ai_explanation_seed: Faraday's Law: induced EMF magnitude = N × rate of change of flux. More turns → more EMF.

subject: Physics
question_text: Light travels from glass (n=1.5) to air (n=1.0). What is the critical angle for total internal reflection?
formula_or_concept: Critical angle: sin(θ_c) = n_rare / n_dense
common_mistakes: Inverting n₁ and n₂
Confusing which medium light is coming from
ai_explanation_seed: TIR occurs when light moves from denser to rarer medium. Critical angle: sin θ_c = n_rare/n_dense.

subject: Physics
question_text: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Where is the image formed?
formula_or_concept: Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u; sign convention: real objects have u negative
common_mistakes: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (mirror formula)
Not applying sign convention for u
ai_explanation_seed: Lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Object on left: u is negative. Positive v means real image on right.

subject: Physics
question_text: In Young's double slit experiment, slit separation d = 0.5 mm, screen distance D = 1 m, wavelength λ = 600 nm. What is the fringe width?
formula_or_concept: Fringe width in YDSE: β = λD/d
common_mistakes: Unit conversion errors (nm to m, mm to m)
Using diameter instead of separation
ai_explanation_seed: YDSE fringe width β = λD/d. Be careful with units: λ in meters, d in meters, D in meters.

subject: Physics
question_text: In the photoelectric effect, what happens when the intensity of light is doubled?
options: A) Kinetic energy of electrons doubles
B) Number of emitted electrons doubles
detailed_solution: Intensity ∝ number of photons per second. More photons → more electrons emitted. KE depends only on frequency, not intensity. Threshold frequency is a material property.
formula_or_concept: Photoelectric effect: KE = hf - φ; intensity affects number of photoelectrons, not their energy
common_mistakes: Thinking higher intensity means higher energy electrons
Confusing intensity with frequency
ai_explanation_seed: KE of photoelectrons depends only on frequency (hf - work function). Intensity controls how many electrons are emitted per second.

subject: Physics
question_text: An electron has kinetic energy 1.6×10⁻¹⁸ J. What is its de Broglie wavelength? (h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J·s, m = 9×10⁻³¹ kg)
formula_or_concept: de Broglie: λ = h/p; for KE given: p = √(2mKE)
common_mistakes: Using λ = h/mv without finding v or p from KE
Arithmetic errors with powers of 10
ai_explanation_seed: Find momentum from KE: p = √(2mKE). Then λ = h/p. Careful with powers of 10.

subject: Physics
question_text: A wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. What is its speed?
formula_or_concept: Wave speed: v = fλ
common_mistakes: Using v = f/λ instead of v = fλ
Confusion about which quantity is given
ai_explanation_seed: Wave equation: speed = frequency × wavelength. v = fλ.

subject: Physics
question_text: A source emitting sound at 1000 Hz moves toward a stationary observer at 30 m/s. What frequency does the observer hear? (Speed of sound = 330 m/s)
formula_or_concept: Doppler formula (source moving toward observer): f' = f × v/(v - v_s)
common_mistakes: Using v+v_s in denominator (source moving away formula)
Confusing observer motion with source motion formulas
ai_explanation_seed: Source approaching observer: apparent frequency increases. f' = f × v/(v - v_s). Note subtraction in denominator.

subject: Physics
question_text: A string of length 1.2 m is fixed at both ends. What is the wavelength of the fundamental mode?
detailed_solution: For fundamental mode in a fixed-fixed string: L = λ/2 → λ = 2L = 2×1.2 = 2.4 m.
formula_or_concept: Fundamental mode: L = λ/2 (both ends fixed); wavelength = 2L
common_mistakes: Using λ = L for fundamental mode
Confusing open and closed pipe formulas with string
ai_explanation_seed: String fixed at both ends: nodes at both ends. Fundamental has half-wavelength fitting in length. λ = 2L.

subject: Physics
question_text: If the mass of Earth is doubled and its radius remains the same, how does the acceleration due to gravity change?
detailed_solution: g = GM/R². If M doubles and R is constant: g doubles.
formula_or_concept: Acceleration due to gravity: g = GM/R²
common_mistakes: Including the object's mass in the formula
Thinking radius change would be involved
ai_explanation_seed: g = GM/R². Only mass of Earth and radius matter. Object mass cancels out.

subject: Physics
question_text: What is the escape velocity from a planet of radius R with surface gravitational acceleration g?
detailed_solution: Setting KE = gravitational PE: ½mv² = GMm/R = m(gR²/R)=mgR → v² = 2gR → v = √(2gR).
formula_or_concept: Escape velocity: v_e = √(2gR) = √(2GM/R)
common_mistakes: Forgetting factor of 2 (only using orbital velocity formula)
Confusing orbital velocity √(gR) with escape velocity √(2gR)
ai_explanation_seed: Escape velocity: set total mechanical energy to zero. ½mv² = GMm/R = mgR → v = √(2gR).

subject: Physics
question_text: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere of mass M and radius R about its diameter is:
detailed_solution: Moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter = (2/5)MR². This is a standard result derived by integration.
formula_or_concept: Solid sphere about diameter: I = (2/5)MR². Other: hollow sphere = (2/3)MR², disk = (1/2)MR²
common_mistakes: Confusing solid sphere with hollow sphere (2/3)
Using disk formula (1/2)MR²
ai_explanation_seed: Standard MI results: solid sphere = 2/5 MR², hollow sphere = 2/3 MR², disk = 1/2 MR². Learn these by heart.

subject: Physics
question_text: Using Gauss's Law, the electric field inside a uniformly charged hollow spherical shell is:
detailed_solution: By Gauss's Law, for a Gaussian surface inside the hollow shell, the enclosed charge q_enc = 0. Therefore E×4πr² = 0 → E = 0.
formula_or_concept: Gauss's Law: ∮E·dA = q_enc/ε₀; no enclosed charge → no field inside
common_mistakes: Thinking the charge on the shell creates a field inside
Applying the point charge formula for r < R
ai_explanation_seed: Gauss's Law: if no charge is enclosed by the Gaussian surface, the net flux is zero → E = 0 everywhere inside a charged hollow shell.

subject: Physics
question_text: In a Wheatstone bridge with P = 3 Ω, Q = 6 Ω, R = 4 Ω, what value of S gives balance?
detailed_solution: Balanced condition: P/Q = R/S → 3/6 = 4/S → S = 4×6/3 = 8 Ω.
formula_or_concept: Wheatstone bridge balance: P/Q = R/S (no current through galvanometer)
common_mistakes: Using P/R = Q/S (wrong arrangement)
Cross multiplying incorrectly
ai_explanation_seed: Wheatstone bridge balanced when P/Q = R/S. Cross multiply to solve for unknown resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which colour of light has the highest speed in a glass medium?
options: D) All colours have same speed
detailed_solution: Red light has the lowest refractive index in glass (least deviation), meaning it travels fastest (v = c/n). Violet has highest n, so lowest speed.
formula_or_concept: v = c/n; lower refractive index → higher speed; red has lowest n in glass
common_mistakes: Thinking violet is fastest because it has higher frequency
Confusing speed in glass with speed in vacuum
ai_explanation_seed: In glass, different colours have different refractive indices (dispersion). Red: n lowest → highest speed. Violet: n highest → lowest speed.

subject: Physics
question_text: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 20 years. After 60 years, what fraction remains?
detailed_solution: Number of half-lives = 60/20 = 3. Fraction remaining = (1/2)³ = 1/8.
formula_or_concept: Radioactive decay: N = N₀(1/2)^(t/T½); after n half-lives: N/N₀ = (1/2)ⁿ
common_mistakes: Dividing by 3 directly instead of using (1/2)^3
Confusing number of half-lives with time
ai_explanation_seed: Count half-lives: t/T½ = 60/20 = 3. After 3 half-lives: 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8 remains.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which process has zero change in entropy for a reversible process?
detailed_solution: For a reversible adiabatic (isentropic) process, Q = 0 → ΔS = Q/T = 0. It is an isentropic process.
formula_or_concept: ΔS = Q/T for reversible process; adiabatic: Q = 0 → ΔS = 0
common_mistakes: Thinking isothermal has zero entropy change (it doesn't — heat is exchanged)
Confusing adiabatic reversible with irreversible adiabatic
ai_explanation_seed: Entropy change ΔS = Q/T. For adiabatic process Q = 0, so ΔS = 0. This is why adiabatic reversible is called isentropic.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 10 μF capacitor is charged to 100 V. What is the energy stored?
formula_or_concept: Energy in capacitor: U = ½CV² = Q²/(2C) = QV/2
common_mistakes: Using U = CV² without the factor of ½
Unit errors with μF
ai_explanation_seed: Energy stored in capacitor = ½CV². Don't forget the factor of ½. Convert μF to F.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two tuning forks of frequency 256 Hz and 260 Hz vibrate simultaneously. How many beats per second are heard?
detailed_solution: Beat frequency = |f₁ - f₂| = |260 - 256| = 4 beats/second.
formula_or_concept: Beat frequency = |f₁ - f₂|
common_mistakes: Adding the frequencies
Dividing the frequencies
ai_explanation_seed: Beats occur due to superposition of two slightly different frequencies. Beat frequency = difference of the two frequencies.

subject: Physics
question_text: A figure skater spinning with arms outstretched pulls her arms in, reducing moment of inertia to half. Her angular velocity:
detailed_solution: Conservation of angular momentum: L = Iω = constant. If I halves, ω doubles.
formula_or_concept: Conservation of angular momentum: Iω = constant (no external torque)
common_mistakes: Thinking angular velocity decreases as they come in
Not applying conservation law (no external torque)
ai_explanation_seed: Angular momentum L = Iω is conserved. If I halves → ω must double to keep L constant.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 100 Ω resistor carries a current of 2 A. What is the power dissipated?
formula_or_concept: Power dissipation: P = I²R = V²/R = IV
common_mistakes: Using P = IR instead of I²R
Using P = V/R formulas incorrectly
ai_explanation_seed: Power in resistor: P = I²R when current is given. Three equivalent forms: P = IV = I²R = V²/R.

subject: Physics
question_text: A proton moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The path of the proton is:
detailed_solution: The magnetic force F = qv×B is always perpendicular to velocity → no work done → speed constant → path is a circle. The radius r = mv/qB.
formula_or_concept: Charged particle perpendicular to B: circular motion, r = mv/(qB)
common_mistakes: Thinking it's a parabola (that's electric field, like projectile)
Thinking force does work and changes speed
ai_explanation_seed: Magnetic force is always ⊥ to velocity → no work → constant speed → circular path. r = mv/qB.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 kg ball moving at 6 m/s collides perfectly inelastically with a 4 kg ball at rest. What is the final velocity of the combined mass?
detailed_solution: By conservation of momentum: m₁v₁ = (m₁+m₂)v'. 2×6 = 6×v'. v' = 12/6 = 2 m/s.
formula_or_concept: Perfectly inelastic collision: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁+m₂)v'; momentum conserved, KE not
common_mistakes: Trying to conserve kinetic energy (it's inelastic)
Not adding masses in the denominator
ai_explanation_seed: Perfectly inelastic: they stick together. Use momentum conservation only: m₁v₁ = (m₁+m₂)v_f.

subject: Physics
question_text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation d is filled with a dielectric of constant K. How does capacitance change?
detailed_solution: C = Kε₀A/d. Introducing dielectric increases capacitance by factor K.
formula_or_concept: Capacitance with dielectric: C = Kε₀A/d; K > 1 always increases capacitance
common_mistakes: Thinking the dielectric reduces capacitance
Squaring K
ai_explanation_seed: Dielectric constant K > 1. C = Kε₀A/d → introducing dielectric multiplies capacitance by K.

subject: Physics
question_text: If a planet's orbital radius increases by a factor of 4, how does its orbital period change?
detailed_solution: Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ r³. T' = T(r'/r)^(3/2) = T×4^(3/2) = T×8. Period increases by 8.
formula_or_concept: Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ a³; T ∝ r^(3/2)
common_mistakes: Using T ∝ r (not r^3/2)
Computing 4² = 16 instead of 4^(3/2) = 8
ai_explanation_seed: Kepler's Third: T ∝ r^(3/2). If r → 4r: T → T × (4)^(3/2) = T × 8.

subject: Physics
question_text: If the intensity of sound doubles, the change in sound level in decibels is approximately:
formula_or_concept: Sound level: L = 10 log(I/I₀); doubling intensity ≈ +3 dB, 10× intensity = +10 dB
common_mistakes: Using 20 log (that's for pressure ratio)
Thinking doubling = +6 dB
ai_explanation_seed: dB change = 10 log(I₂/I₁). Doubling intensity: 10 log 2 ≈ 3 dB. Tenfold: 10 log 10 = 10 dB.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball is thrown upward with velocity 20 m/s. What is the maximum height reached? (g = 10 m/s²)
detailed_solution: At max height, v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gh: 0 = 400 - 2×10×h → h = 400/20 = 20 m.
formula_or_concept: v² = u² - 2gh; at max height v = 0
common_mistakes: Forgetting that v = 0 at maximum height
Using h = v/g instead of v²/(2g)
ai_explanation_seed: At max height velocity = 0. Use v² = u² - 2gh with v = 0 → h = u²/(2g).

subject: Physics
question_text: A block of mass 10 kg is on a smooth horizontal surface. Forces of 30 N (east) and 40 N (north) act on it simultaneously. What is the net acceleration?
formula_or_concept: Resultant of perpendicular forces: F_net = √(F₁² + F₂²); then a = F/m
common_mistakes: Adding forces algebraically (3+4=7) instead of using Pythagoras
Finding components instead of resultant first
ai_explanation_seed: Perpendicular forces: resultant by Pythagoras. F_net = √(30² + 40²) = 50 N. a = F/m = 5 m/s².

subject: Physics
question_text: The rms speed of gas molecules is proportional to:
detailed_solution: v_rms = √(3RT/M). So v_rms ∝ √T (at constant molar mass M).
formula_or_concept: RMS speed: v_rms = √(3RT/M) ∝ √T
common_mistakes: Thinking v_rms ∝ T (missing square root)
Including pressure in the relationship
ai_explanation_seed: RMS speed formula: v = √(3RT/M). Temperature appears under square root, so v ∝ √T.

subject: Physics
question_text: A solenoid of length 0.5 m has 1000 turns and carries 2 A. The magnetic field inside is (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A):
formula_or_concept: Solenoid field: B = μ₀nI = μ₀(N/L)I
common_mistakes: Using N instead of n = N/L
Forgetting to divide turns by length
ai_explanation_seed: B = μ₀nI where n = turns per unit length = N/L. Not N directly.
